title: SPARKLE: A Structured and Plug-and-play Agentic Retrieval Policy for Adaptive RAG Models
abstract: SPARKLE trains a proxy-model controller with reinforcement learning and structured knowledge-graph reasoning to make adaptive retrieval-policy decisions independently of the downstream retriever and language model.

admission.reason: The abstract establishes an adaptive retrieval-policy controller, but it does not show explicit evidence-gap representation, evidence sufficiency or abstention, temporal/version constraints, calibrated stopping, or resource-bounded completion. Its marginal contribution to the open gaps is weaker than the verified candidates that combine decomposition with iterative bounded evaluation. The identifier is also UNCHECKED, so there is no reason to prefer it over stronger verified evidence at this gate.

title: Test-time Corpus Feedback: From Retrieval to RAG
abstract: This survey organizes adaptive retrieval and ranking methods by where test-time feedback originates and whether it updates the query, retrieved context, or document pool, emphasizing retrieval as an iterative and learnable component rather than a one-shot RAG stage.

admission.reason: This is a survey taxonomy of test-time retrieval feedback. It may be useful for orientation, but the abstract does not itself validate a structured evidence-gap controller, stopping criterion, provenance mechanism, or risk guarantee and therefore does not materially close an open research stream in this round. The identity is UNCHECKED as well.

title: Interpretable Uncertainty for Adaptive Retrieval and Reasoning in Question Answering
abstract: The method decomposes uncertainty into knowledge insufficiency and ambiguity or conflict, using the former to trigger retrieval and the latter to trigger additional reasoning, thereby tying adaptive actions to interpretable uncertainty signals.

admission.reason: Separating knowledge insufficiency from ambiguity or conflict is relevant, but the abstract only shows that different uncertainty types trigger retrieval versus reasoning. It does not demonstrate calibrated answerability, bounded-risk stopping, explicit terminal-state semantics, or provenance/time handling. The current round has more direct candidates for both evidence-sufficiency evaluation and risk-controlled stopping, so this does not add enough marginal evidence for a reading slot.

title: Adaptive Retrieval Without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home
abstract: This systematic empirical study compares adaptive retrieval approaches with numerous uncertainty-estimation methods across question-answering quality, self-knowledge, and efficiency, finding that uncertainty signals can often provide competitive adaptive-retrieval decisions without complex pipelines.

admission.reason: The systematic comparison of uncertainty signals is relevant to adaptive retrieval, but the abstract evaluates retrieval decisions, self-knowledge, and efficiency rather than the open questions about structured gaps, iterative sufficiency, calibrated stopping under shift, temporal/version provenance, or terminal-state discrimination. It is therefore supportive background rather than a gap-closing contribution. The identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: Towards Adaptive Memory-Based Optimization for Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Amber combines an agent-memory updater, adaptive information collector, and filtering mechanism so that retrieval queries evolve with accumulated evidence and information collection can terminate when the system judges that enough knowledge has been gathered.

admission.reason: The abstract describes evolving retrieval queries and termination when the system judges that enough knowledge has been collected, but it does not expose a calibrated sufficiency criterion, a bounded-risk guarantee, temporal/version provenance, explicit failure states, or cost-aware stopping. This is another heuristic adaptive-collection loop, whereas the unresolved gaps now concern reliability and composition beyond that capability.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: The paper studies selective classification across covariate, label, and out-of-distribution shifts and analyzes confidence-scoring strategies through their risk-coverage tradeoffs, providing transfer evidence for calibrated abstention under non-IID deployment.

admission.reason: Selective classification under covariate, label, and out-of-distribution shifts is valid transfer evidence for F7, but it is generic classification rather than sequential retrieval or structured generation. The current candidate set contains substantially closer conformal and selective-prediction papers that address structured outputs, adaptive stopping, and prompt/domain shift, so this paper has insufficient marginal value for this reading round.

title: Principled Context Engineering for RAG: Statistical Guarantees via Conformal Prediction
abstract: The paper applies conformal prediction to retrieved-context selection, filtering noisy material while targeting statistical coverage of relevant evidence and thereby providing a principled reliability layer for RAG context construction.

admission.reason: Conformal coverage for selecting retrieved context is relevant to reliable context construction, but the abstract does not establish answerability, abstention, iterative stopping, distribution-shift adaptation, or version-aware evidence sufficiency. Guaranteeing that selected context covers relevant evidence is not the same as deciding that accumulated evidence is sufficient to answer or that retrieval should stop.

title: Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework
abstract: This work treats refusal as a mechanism for controlling RAG risk and uses counterfactual prompting to probe retrieval quality and the model's use of evidence, introducing evaluation with abstention and risk-oriented metrics.

admission.reason: The paper treats refusal as RAG risk control and evaluates retrieval quality and evidence use, which is relevant to F3, but the abstract does not show iterative retrieval stopping, distribution-shift robustness, structured sufficiency, or the terminal-state distinctions now open. The evidence-sufficiency benchmark and conformal stopping candidates provide more direct marginal value for the present gaps.

title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
abstract: Adaptive-RAG learns to route questions among no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval strategies according to predicted question complexity, providing a direct adaptive controller over retrieval depth.

admission.reason: Routing questions among no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval is an important adaptive-RAG baseline, but the abstract bases the decision on predicted question complexity rather than explicit evidence state and does not provide iterative sufficiency assessment, risk-controlled stopping, temporal/version handling, or resource-aware terminal semantics. It does not materially close the remaining gaps.

title: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Conversational Systems
abstract: The paper introduces RAGate, which predicts for each conversational turn whether external retrieval is needed rather than always invoking RAG, using human judgments of retrieval necessity to train and evaluate the gate.

admission.reason: RAGate predicts whether a conversational turn needs external retrieval, but this is a one-stage retrieval-necessity gate. The abstract does not show multi-round evidence acquisition, reassessment after retrieval, structured missing-information representation, stopping reliability, or provenance constraints, so it does not materially advance the open Topic 07 gaps.

title: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift
abstract: This work studies selective question answering when deployment data mixes in-domain and out-of-domain examples, evaluating calibrators through risk-coverage behavior and showing why abstention calibration becomes difficult under domain shift.

admission.reason: Selective QA under mixed in-domain and out-of-domain deployment is relevant transfer evidence for calibration under shift, but it does not concern iterative retrieval or evidence acquisition. Newer admitted candidates directly address structured generation, drift adaptation, and sequential stopping, leaving this older QA result with insufficient marginal value for the current reading round.

title: When to Retrieve During Reasoning: Adaptive Retrieval for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: ReaLM-Retrieve detects step-level knowledge gaps during reasoning and learns a retrieval-intervention policy that decides when external evidence should be acquired instead of retrieving at fixed intervals.

admission.reason: Detecting step-level knowledge gaps and deciding when to retrieve is directly relevant to F2, but the abstract does not show a structured representation of the missing evidence, post-retrieval sufficiency reassessment, calibrated stopping, temporal/version provenance, or budget-aware terminal conditions. Generic adaptive retrieval timing is no longer the principal unresolved capability in this round.

title: CtrlA: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inherent Control
abstract: CtrlA extracts representation-level signals associated with model honesty and confidence and uses them to control when retrieval should occur and how retrieval queries should be formulated.

admission.reason: CtrlA uses internal honesty and confidence representations to decide when to retrieve and how to formulate queries, but the abstract does not demonstrate iterative evidence-state updates, explicit sufficiency or abstention semantics, calibrated risk under shift, provenance, or resource-bounded stopping. It therefore adds little to the specific unresolved gaps beyond established adaptive-retrieval gating.

title: Knowing You Don't Know: Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round RAG through Self-Practicing
abstract: SIM-RAG trains a lightweight information-sufficiency critic through self-practicing so that each retrieval round can decide whether accumulated evidence is sufficient or whether search should continue.

admission.reason: A learned information-sufficiency critic for deciding whether multi-round RAG should continue is directly relevant, but the round's remaining stopping gap is specifically about calibration drift, unsafe early stopping, conservative over-retrieval, and bounded-risk behavior under distribution shift. The abstract provides no calibration guarantee, shift evaluation, provenance constraint, or differentiated terminal-state model, so it mainly reinforces a capability the gap statement already treats as established.
